# Flux Builds AI — Clipper Kit prompts

Use your own or authorized footage. Paste a timecoded transcript plus your own moment notes. These prompts help plan edits; they do not verify the footage, rights, or likely view count. Check every timestamp against the actual source.

## RADAR — shortlist moments
From this timecoded transcript and my notes, nominate up to five moments with a complete setup and payoff. For each, give source in/out, the exact evidence for the payoff, missing visual context to review, and why a new viewer might care. Mark uncertain timestamps. Do not invent moments or claim to have watched footage from a transcript alone.

## HOOK — three honest openings
Write three short opening options for this actual event: [context]. The obstacle was [obstacle]. The actual outcome was [payoff]. Audience: [audience]. One should emphasize stakes, one surprise, and one a useful question. Use only supported information. Do not invent a quote, outcome, metric, or deadline. State what picture must accompany each opening.

## BATCH — plan complete small stories
Using my reviewed shortlist, create an edit plan. Each clip needs source ID, in/out, opening, minimum context, payoff, and crop or caption notes. Avoid duplicate payoffs. Keep qualifications and reactions that affect meaning. Rank by story clarity and available evidence, not a made-up viral probability.

## NICHE — transfer the story shape
My niche is [gaming / podcast / education / fitness / other]. My authorized material is [description]. Propose five clip angles using promise, obstacle, and visible result. Include an illustrative opening and the context that must remain. Do not invent what happened. For fitness or specialist advice, retain the relevant limitations and speaker qualifications.

## AUDIT — critique the actual cut
Review this supplied clip or, if only a transcript is available, explicitly limit the review to text. Check opening clarity, context, payoff, quote integrity, portrait framing, caption readability/timing, dialogue audibility, sound-off comprehension, ending, and the tested resource route. Return timestamped concrete fixes and mark unavailable evidence. Do not forecast views.
